A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Integrator subunit 4 (INTS4) is a Symplekin-like scaffolding protein that interacts with the catalytic core (INTS9 and INTS11) of the Integrator complex and is required for UsnRNA 5′-end processing.
INTS4, INTS9, and INTS11 are the ‘cleavage module’, while the remaining INT subunits are the ‘processing module’.

the INTS9/INTS11/INTS4 complex represents a ‘cleavage module’, similar to the CPSF73/CPSF100/Symplekin complex that is responsible for the endonucleolyic activity of the Integrator complex.
INTS4, like Symplekin, acts as an integrator scaffold protein to bring together the catalytic core and the RNA binding subunits.
